papers_read.title_as_printed: Pack file pdf/P-114.txt is 'A method for diagnosis support of mild cognitive impairment through EEG rhythms source location during working memory tasks' (San-Martin et al., BSPC 66 (2021) 102499), which is P-112's paper (P-113 is its dedup stub). The paper the record means (claim '93% Acc', registry row 'Kinect V2 tracking, gait feature engineering, ANFIS', summaries.md header 1-s2.0-S1746809421003195) is 'Detection of mild cognitive Impairment from gait using Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference system' (Seifallahi et al., BSPC 71 (2022) 103195), which is in the pack as pdf/P-115.txt. Both files were read in full; the verdict uses the gait paper.
Using a dual-stream attention neural network to characterize mild cognitive impairment based on retinal images (Gao et al., Computers in Biology and Medicine 166 (2023) 107411)

what_each_reports.P-114: Kinect V2 skeletal gait features (single-task, dual-task, dual-task cost) from 150 Iranian older adults (70 MCI, 80 HC, IDAA Tehran); hierarchical ANFIS vs LR and SVM. Best result: ANFIS on all 26 dual-task-walking features, accuracy 93%, sensitivity 90%, precision 98.66%, specificity 99%, F-score 91.5% (Table 6). Single-task ANFIS accuracy 86.87%. The paper does not state the train/test or cross-validation protocol used for the ANFIS figures (five-fold validation is mentioned only for SVM hyperparameter search).
what_each_reports.P-5: Dual-stream cross-fusion attention network (DuCAN) on paired fundus photographs and OCT images. First dataset (29 MCI, 50 CN, 38 AD patients; image-level, 5-fold CV): three-class AD/MCI/CN accuracy 91.64%, AUC 96.78%; for the MCI class within the three-class model, precision 84.96%, recall 88.08%, specificity 95.46%, F1 85.68% (Table 2). Second dataset (133 nCI vs 140 pCI by MMSE/MoCA, transfer learning): accuracy 82.46%, AUC 84.41%, pCI precision 70.9% (Table 3; the abstract gives 80.90% for this).

quantity_a: Accuracy of an ANFIS classifier on Kinect dual-task gait features for binary MCI vs healthy control, 150 participants from one Iranian association, evaluation protocol unstated
quantity_b: Per-class precision (positive predictive value) for the MCI class inside a three-class AD/MCI/CN deep-learning classifier on multimodal retinal images, image-level 5-fold CV, one Chinese hospital cohort
incompatible_if_same: No. Even read as two performance figures, 93% accuracy and 84.96% precision are different metrics computed from different confusion matrices; neither study claims a value or ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: mismatch: P-114 is binary MCI vs HC (T1); P-5's 84.96% is a per-class figure from a three-class AD/MCI/CN model (the registry itself codes P-5 as T2)
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: own IDAA Tehran cohort vs own Daping Hospital/Wenzhou cohort; no waiver on record (the record's dataset_equal='Yes' is wrong)
gates.validation_tier: uncertain/mismatch: P-5 internal 5-fold CV at image level; P-114 states no ANFIS evaluation protocol
gates.modality_family: mismatch: gait/motor (Kinect skeletal tracking) vs retinal imaging (fundus + OCT); no waiver on record

performance_validity: flag does not apply: neither registry row trips it and no contested figure reaches 0.97 (P-5's AUC is 96.78%; P-114's 98.66% precision and 99% specificity are not the contested accuracy). It is nominally a performance comparison but across different metrics.
independence: Independent: different groups, countries, cohorts and modalities; no shared authors.
grounds: P-5's 84.96% is the precision for the MCI class of a three-class AD/MCI/CN retinal-image model, not a binary MCI-detection accuracy, so the metric type differs from P-114's 93% accuracy.
The class contrast differs: P-114 separates MCI from healthy controls only, while P-5's figure comes from a model that also has to separate AD.
The modality-family gate fails (Kinect gait vs fundus/OCT) and the dataset-family gate fails (separate own cohorts in Iran and China), with no waiver on record.

The record's own resolution note already names the metric incommensurability (Acc vs Precision); the status false_positive understates it, since the two figures are on different quantities rather than compatible values of one quantity.

evidence_quotes.quote: the proposed ANFIS classifier had values of 93%, 90%, and 91.5% for accuracy, sensitivity, and F-score, respectively when all extracted gait parameters in the DTW condition for the classification of elderly subjects to MCI and HC groups.
Of 150 selected subjects, 80 subjects were healthy individuals without any cognitive impairments (HC subjects), and 70 subjects were elderly people with MCI.
The MCI subjects of the present study were selected through clients of the Iran dementia and Alzheimer's Association (IDAA) in Tehran city of Iran
The proposed method achieved high precision rates of 84.96% and 80.90% in classifying MCI and positive test scores for cognitive impairment, respectively.
As shown in Table 2, the proposed network DuCAN had an accuracy of 91.64% and an AUC of 96.78%.
The first dataset included information for a total of 29 patients (58 eyes) with MCI, 50 age-matched individuals with CN (100 eyes), and 38 patients (76 eyes) with AD.

record_defects: The pack's PDF for P-114 (and data/paper_pdf_map.json, method 'formula-unverified') points at the San-Martin EEG paper (DOI 10.1016/j.bspc.2021.102499, P-112's paper); the record's P-114 is the Seifallahi gait/ANFIS paper (DOI 10.1016/j.bspc.2021.103195), whose PDF the map assigns to P-115.
claim_b 'P-5: 84.96% precision on T1' mislabels the task: 84.96% is the MCI-class precision of a three-class AD/MCI/CN model.
dataset_equal='Yes' and validation_comparable='Yes' are wrong: separate own cohorts; P-114 states no ANFIS evaluation protocol.
The bridging-evidence list (31 papers, P-360, P-322) is generic and bears on neither paper's quantity.
C-26 and C-29 are the same pair (C-29's paper_b was repointed from the P-10 stub to P-5 on 2026-08-29), so the ledger counts this pair twice.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these two papers: a comparable pair would need a binary MCI-vs-HC accuracy from P-5 (it reports none) in the same modality and cohort family as P-114.
